state.context: Invoice currently exports only the sales payload and inbound capability. Bookings can prove their completion and memberships their cancellation boundary; neither owns the other product history. Actual money evidence belongs to Invoice. Refer currently recognizes exclusive program and different account, but has no verified capture clock or first-sale rule. Visiting a public code proves neither identity nor a purchase. Changes here describe executable draft scenarios, not provider/runtime implementation.
state.candidate: Use Invoice as the shared customer-commercial-history authority, retaining an explicit complete-history baseline and refusing unknown historical state. Refer writes immutable captures under verified customer permission; the latest still-valid capture wins. A booking/term freezes that capture and reports its own milestone. Invoice checks that immutable commercial source against billed customer/amount and real receipts/refunds before broadcasting Qualification. Ordered revisions, source identity checks and reversal tombstones protect reordered/replayed messages.

ownership.instructions: Which placement most directly supports private, evidenced first-customer rules across products while keeping the authored workflow and replay obligations small?

criteria.invoice: Centralize the first-customer judgement in Invoice using actual payment records, upstream milestones and Refer captures. Adds precise producer handoffs and historical review but avoids two competing customer histories.
criteria.source: Have both product owners classify first customers using their local records. Simpler isolated source handlers need an additional reliable cross-product history synchronization before their answers can agree.
criteria.consumer: Trust the incoming captured timestamp and first_customer assertion inside Refer. Minimal receiver logic requires a real trusted producer to carry the entire authoritative-history obligation.
